newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Morgan Stanley classify Portugal as developed mkt.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley classify Portugal as developed mkt.

text.p: The Geneva-based Capital International Perspective, which calculates the Morgan Stanley Capital International Indices (MSCI), said Portugal will be switched from its emerging markets index to its developed market index.
The change will take place on December 2, 1997.

The company said in a statement that the change marked "recognition of Portugal's overall economic development, its macro-economic and financial policies, as well as its equity market characteristics."
"Its characterisation as emerging is no longer appropriate," it added.
The move, which had long been expected, should lead to greater foreign interest in the Portuguese stock market by international funds, analysts said.
The statement said that Portugal's gross domestic product (GDP) exceeded the threshold used by the World Bank to categorise high-income countries.
Portugal had been carrying out structural reforms to its economy and was among leading candidates to form part of the European Union's single currency at its launch in 1999.
While the equity market was still modest in size, it had been expanding in terms of capitalisation, the statement said.
"All the above improvements have positively impacted international investors' confidence," it said.
